newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam may grant Hyundai vehicle plant licence.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam may grant Hyundai vehicle plant licence.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd could get a licence to build a vehicle assembly plant in southern Vietnam if Chrysler Corp gives up a licence it was granted in 1995, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

"I think there would be a better chance for Hyundai," Deputy Minister for Industry Nguyen Xuan Chuan told Reuters. He said that Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet still felt no more licences should be issued to carmakers in addition to the 14 already granted.

Officials at the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) were not available to comment on Chrysler, which local newspapers says has relinquished its plans for a $192 million assembly plant near Ho Chi Minh City.
Chrysler's regional office in Bangkok declined to comment on whether it was pulling out from the project, whose licence from the MPI will expire in July if not taken up.

However, the MPI-run Vietnam Investment Review quoted Chrysler spokeswoman Jodi Armstrong as saying that the U.S. firm had walked away from the project because Vietnam had issued many licences to carmakers.

"Anywhere between 10,000 and 50,000 units annual split between 14 manufacturers doesn't make a very attractive picture," she said. "They've granted assembly licences to anybody and their brother who wants to build a vehicle in Vietnam."
Chuan said sales of all vehicles totalled 37,000 units last year, with cars accounting for around 35 percent of the total. He forecast the market will grow by at least 27 percent this year.
